chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: The drunken Hollywood session with Butch Luckett and Hunter Gray
summary: Rene brings in replacements, but the musicians turn up drunk, and the session yields only a few weak sides such as Strolling After School.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: One thing I mention casually about Harry Burn--
That's the story.

Anyway, as I said, we were headed back out there so we're at the point where Rene comes up, we're going to do a session and so, he says we haven't gotten to In The Mood yet, we're going to do something other than In The Mood. We were kind of talking about In The Mood.
In this session we had Hunter Gray, we had Butch and he comes up with--do you know the guitar player that was with the Nat Cole Trio?
Yes, Oscar Moore.
So anyway--
And then they had ma dear friend, later--oh, gee, go ahead.

Well anyway, we go in and are going to do a session, several numbers and Rene said to me, I do so much recording around here, I think it would be better if you use your man, so it would be a different sound, you know, it won't be the same thing, and he said I heard Butch and everything and he's all right.
So we said okay. We got set up and that night when we went to record Butchie didn't come because he was drinking.
But as it turned out, old "Shoe Sole"--Hunter Gray was around the corner--
Good reader.
He was drunk.
And Rene had worked in the band with Hunter, he had never worked with Butch and he said, my goodness, why would you do that,
Who was called 'Shoe Sole'?
Hunter Gray.
That was his nickname?
Yeah, nickname.
Rene said I'll call in some guys out here. So he called in--I don't know which one of them deals it was, but whichever one was there, which I didn't know, but he was a liquor head.
Yes, I'll recall his name in a minute, we played a million recording dates together.

So anyway, Earl Palmer (phonetic spelling) was there and this guy got drunk, and Earl said Ernie, you're going to think Rene's got your money and I said what do you mean, he said well, you thought he was going to do better, him telling you he's going to get a good musician and he comes up
with another liquor head. He said I don't believe they want to play with you.

So anyway we fooled around and we made a number or two but we just didn't like the way, we said it's not going to do anything--I still have one, Strolling After School and several of them we did, but we saw that they weren't going anywhere, and we didn't even try because we were paying for this.
